title: Sam Parr on copywriting: long-form, AIDA, plain writing and copy work
summary: Sam explains why he obsessed over copywriting (sales on paper scales one-to-one selling) and which timeless principles still work: long copy, AIDA, fourth-grade writing, and hand-copying great sales pages. He also argues for leading with a feeling and the founder's story.

principles.text: Copywriting is sales on paper: it scales one-to-one selling to an unlimited audience.
principles.quote: if I could take my ability to sell one-to-one, which I eventually learned how to do, and put it on paper, you could sell one to an infinite number.

principles.text: Long copy usually beats short copy; the real enemy is boring, not length.
principles.quote: There's no such thing as too long. There's only such a thing as too uninteresting.

principles.text: Structure copy as AIDA (attention, interest, desire, action) so readers slide to one specific next step.
principles.quote: I want you to fall down this slippery slope where you start where you're interested, you get a little bit more desire, and finally I get you to take action.

principles.text: Write simply at a 4th-5th grade level (use Hemingway App), in active voice, without adverbs.
principles.quote: The goal is to write at a fourth or fifth grade reading level.

principles.text: Train by copy work: hand-write great sales pages or books word for word to absorb their texture.
principles.quote: You write it word for word. And you feel the texture of the words and that changes your brain and it changes what you do.

principles.text: Lead a page with a feeling and the founder's personal story, not a feature list.
principles.quote: Above the fold should be a feeling, I think.
